review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped the repo for other copies of the identification familyGroup (fun _ : PUnit => a) = toralRootGroup tau K a. It appears only in this file's two theorems, so there is no existing lemma to reuse. The repeated block is small (about 5 lines), so the finding is modest. The other proofs (finiteIndex_toralRootGroup and the perfect-group commutator argument) have no repeated machinery. I did not open the definitions of familyGroup, familyKernel or toralRootGroup, so I haven't checked that the proposed helper's proof, which just copies the existing one, behaves the same outside the two current contexts. I have not compiled the proposed lemma.

findings.problem: Two theorems each reprove the same identification of the singleton-family group with the toral root group. The proof has two steps: show familyKernel is rootCharKernel by ext and simp, then unfold familyGroup and toralRootGroup. The copy at lines 42-46 is verbatim the same as the one at lines 29-33. Both are written as a local `have he` with the same nested `hker`. A change to the definitions of familyGroup, familyKernel or toralRootGroup would have to be fixed in both places. The identification is also a reusable fact that has no name.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma before line 25, in the same namespace with the same variables: `theorem familyGroup_const_punit_eq_toralRootGroup {tau : Tag} {K : Type} [Field K] (a : Fin tau.rank → Kˣ) : familyGroup (fun _ : PUnit => a) = toralRootGroup tau K a`. Its proof is the existing body (the `hker` ext/simp, then `simp only [familyGroup, toralRootGroup, hker]`). Then `isPointClosed_toralRootGroup` becomes `simpa only [familyGroup_const_punit_eq_toralRootGroup a] using isPointClosed_familyGroup (fun _ : PUnit => a)`. In `closedIdentityComponent_toralCentralizer_eq`, `hc` becomes `simpa only [familyGroup_const_punit_eq_toralRootGroup a] using closedIdentityComponent_familyGroup (fun _ : PUnit => a)`. The `he` blocks at lines 29-33 and 42-46 are deleted. The rewritten uses keep their hypotheses: `[IsAlgClosed K]` is needed only by the two family lemmas, not by the new lemma. Whether `simpa only` accepts the lemma in place of the local `he` is untested.
findings.benefit: The 5-line proof is stated once, so the two main proofs show only the real mathematical step: the family result applied to a singleton family. A later change to the family definitions then needs one fix instead of two. The new lemma name documents the identification, and other files can reuse it.
